facts.statement: The skeleton of a small ceratopsian was discovered on the westbank of the river Tuanhe in Neixiang, Henan.
facts.quote: On the westbank of the river Tuanhe in Neixiang in Henan the skeleton was discovered of a small ceratopian.

facts.statement: The specific name azumai honors the Japanese paleontologist Yoichi Azuma, who discovered Archaeoceratops.
facts.quote: The specific name honours the Japanese paleontologist Yoichi Azuma, the discoverer of Archaeoceratops.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen ZMNH M8856 was found in a layer of the Xiaguan Formation dating from the Turonian to Campanian stages.
facts.quote: The holotype, ZMNH M8856, was found in a layer of the Xiaguan Formation dating from the Turonian-Campanian.

facts.statement: Mosaiceratops can be distinguished by four unique derived traits: a groove between the premaxilla and maxilla, an elongated anterior jugal with parallel edges, two small bumps on the jugal below the eye sockets, and an obliquely pointed rear blade of the ilium.
facts.quote: It can be distinguished by four autapomorphic, unique derived traits: the presence of an evident groove between the premaxilla and the maxilla in lateral view; the elongation of the anterior part of the jugal having a parallel upper edge and lower edge; the main body of the jugal below the eye sockets bears two small bumps; in the ilium the extremity of the upper edge of the rear blade is pointed obliquely to above and behind.

facts.statement: The premaxilla of Mosaiceratops is edentulous, meaning it lacks teeth.
facts.quote: The premaxilla is edentulous, meaning it lacks teeth.

facts.statement: The jugal bone of Mosaiceratops is formed as an inverted T.
facts.quote: The jugal bone is formed as an inverted T.

facts.statement: Mosaiceratops lived during the late Cretaceous, approximately 94 to 72 million years ago, from the Turonian to Campanian stages, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 94 a 72 millones de años, desde el Turoniense al Campaniense, en lo que es hoy Asia

facts.statement: It is debated whether Mosaiceratops is the most basal neoceratopsian or the sister taxon to Psittacosaurus, which would reinstate the family name Psittacosauridae.
facts.quote: However, they noted that this position was not strongly supported in their phylogenetic analysis, acknowledging the possibility that Mosaiceratops instead represents the sister taxon to Psittacosaurus (in which case the name Psittacosauridae would be reinstated).

facts.statement: In Mosaiceratops, the premaxilla is toothless, meaning it has a horny edge.
facts.quote: En Mosaiceratops, el premaxilar es desdentado, lo que significa que tiene un borde correoso.

facts.statement: The holotype is represented by an incomplete and disarticulated skeleton including pelvis and leg bones, 24 vertebrae, a dorsal rib, a humerus, a radius, and the anterior articulated part of the skull with disarticulated postorbital and squamosal bones.
facts.quote: El holotipo está representado por un esqueleto incompleto y desarticulado que incluye huesos de la pelvis y de las patas (fémur, tibia, peroné, isquion, ilion, algunas falanges y metatarsos, el calcáneo y el astrágalo), 24 vértebras (3 cervicales, 3 dorsales y 18 caudales), una costilla dorsal, un húmero, un radio y la parte anterior articulada del cráneo con los huesos postorbital y escamosal desarticulados.

facts.statement: The articulated part of the skull preserves the rostral bone, premaxilla, maxilla, jugal, quadratojugal, dentary, surangular, angular bone, anterior section of the prefrontal bone, and anterior part of the nasal bone.
facts.quote: La parte articulada del cráneo preserva el hueso rostral, el premaxilar, el maxilar, el yugal, cuadratoyugal, dentario, surangular, el hueso angular, la sección anterior del hueso prefrontal, y la parte anterior del hueso nasal.
